case_title: Harilal Etc. v. State of Madhya Pradesh (Now Chhattisgarh)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to imprisonment for life
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that three individuals assaulted and killed a man during a night incident. A first information report (FIR) was lodged the next day by a village chowkidar, who was not an eyewitness. Two eyewitnesses testified about the incident, but their accounts were inconsistent with previous statements and lacked details about the severity of the assault. The body was found near a temple, 300 feet away from where the assault allegedly occurred. Medical evidence indicated severe injuries, including head trauma and rib fractures, suggesting a violent attack. The prosecution relied on the discovery of a lathi and blood-stained clothes at the accused's residences, but the evidence was inconclusive regarding the cause of death and the exact manner in which the assault occurred. The courts found that the prosecution failed to establish the genesis of the crime and the manner in which the murder took place, leading to the acquittal of the accused.
